title: fix(control-ui): old tabs 404 on lazy chunks for seconds after the Gateway restarts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-open Control UI tab from the previous build gets 404s for its lazy `assets/*` chunks for several seconds after the Gateway restarts (for example right after `openclaw update`), so opening a not-yet-loaded view fails even though that generation is retained on disk.

## User Impact

User impact: right after a Gateway restart, an old tab's lazy chunk request waits for the retained-generation check to finish, then gets the retained bytes, instead of failing with "Importing a module script failed". Chunks of the current build and cached responses never wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained generations (#129922, #131930) are invisible until `prepare()` finishes re-verifying every retained generation's bytes. On a loaded host that took 5–17 s after ready, and until then `resolveAsset()` returned null and the HTTP path 404'd immediately.

The retention owner now makes `resolveAsset` async. On a miss while a preparation's inventory phase is running, it joins that phase (success, failure, or abort all release it) and looks up once more. It waits only for inventory, not for the later publication and prune. The wait needs no new timer: preparation is already bounded by the retained-cache limits and aborts on lifecycle stop, disable, and Gateway restart drain, which releases waiters with a miss. Verification checks, limits, publication, and prune behavior are unchanged. There is no new config and no new persisted state.

The optional "let inventory yield to foreground work" idea is not part of this PR. Stale-tab requests now wait on the inventory, so slowing it would lengthen that wait, and no interleaved A/B shows a first-visible win.

Known separate limitation, not changed here: today's Control UI build is ~53 MB per generation (1,434 manifest assets: ~33.5 MB JS plus ~18 MB `.br`/`.gz` sidecars). That means the 96 MiB budget cannot keep the current generation plus a full prior one, and the post-update prune removes the prior generation. Chunks served before the prune keep coming from the per-root in-memory cache; chunks first requested after the prune still miss. This is being handled in a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

**Live, full isolated Gateway** (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, isolated state dir and port, auto-resolved bundled root). Before each restart, two prior generations of the real `pnpm ui:build` output were published through `createControlUiAssetRetention().prepare()` (1,436 files / 53.4 MB retained). The probe requested the newest prior generation's unique lazy chunk every 50 ms starting the instant `/readyz` reported ready. Host load was 35–100, which makes the window long.

| Run | 404s before first 200 | ready → first 200 | first-request latency | 404s after first 200 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main, run 1 | 71 | 6.4 s | 0.6 s (404) | – |
| main, run 2 | 168 | 14.5 s | 1.2 s (404) | – |
| main, run 3 | 112 | 10.5 s | 0.4 s (404) | – |
| main, extended probe | 130 | 12.4 s | 1.5 s (404) | 0 |
| this PR, run 1 | **0** | 17.1 s | 17.1 s (held, then 200) | 0 |
| this PR, run 2 | **0** | 5.1 s | 5.1 s (held, then 200) | 0 |
| this PR, run 3 | **0** | 14.0 s | 14.0 s (held, then 200) | 0 |

The extended probes kept polling until the `sidecars.control-ui-assets` startup trace plus 3 s.

**Regression tests (fail on main, pass here):**

- `src/gateway/control-ui-retained-assets.http.test.ts`: "waits for retained inventory before serving a stale bundled asset" drives the real retention owner and the real HTTP handler, with the inventory held at the prior generation's asset read by a deterministic gate (no timers). On main: `AssertionError: expected 404 to be 200`. The existing retained-generation HTTP case moved into this file unchanged, because `control-ui.http.test.ts` is over the line-cap ratchet. That file shrinks by 35 lines.
- `src/gateway/control-ui-asset-retention.cancellation.test.ts`: "releases a pending retained asset lookup when inventory is aborted" checks that a pending lookup resolves `null` and `prepare()` rejects with the abort. On main the lookup settled while the inventory was still held.

Test cost with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, timed on a host at load 35–100, so walls are dominated by compile and contention: new `control-ui-retained-assets.http.test.ts` 133 s (both cases together run in under 1 s), and the new cancellation case 0.4 s.

**Gates:** these pass:

- `pnpm run tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:test:root`
- `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `check:madge-import-cycles`
- `check:line-cap-ratchet --base origin/main`
- `oxfmt --check` and typed oxlint on all changed files; the lint invocation was proven live by a planted `no-floating-promises` violation
- focused suites: all `control-ui-asset-retention*`, `control-ui.http`, `control-ui-retained-assets.http`, `server-control-ui-root.resolve` and `.identity`

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` fails only on the inherited `agents-other: 726 test roots exceeds the advisory 720 limit` shard budget. That reproduces on the untouched base `c0c8fc9a39a6` and is already fixed on current main by `4f0541eb4691`.
